candidate_findings.title: The mandated runner call shape may violate the generic Sized bound
candidate_findings.gap: The proposed generic has Rust's implicit Sized bound, while the concrete ExecutionEngine call dereferences a runner container before borrowing it. candidate_findings.missing_contract: Specify the actual ExecutionEngine runner type and require either `R: PlatformRunner + ?Sized`, `&dyn PlatformRunner`, or a concrete-type-preserving call, with a compile test using the real field type.

candidate_findings.title: Cleanup is sequential prose rather than a guaranteed lifecycle invariant
candidate_findings.gap: The plan says to await execution, then await cleanup, but defines no guard or structured cancellation behavior. Cancellation or panic before the cleanup await skips cleanup; an implementation using early propagation can also skip it on runner error. It also does not define which error is returned when execution and cleanup both fail.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The wrapper's central promise fails exactly on abnormal paths where process and temporary-resource cleanup is most important.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define a cancellation-safe lifecycle mechanism, require cleanup after both Ok and Err execution results, specify panic/abort handling where feasible, define execution-versus-cleanup error precedence, and add failure/cancellation acceptance tests.

candidate_findings.title: Recursive directory-mtime pruning can erase newer or active evidence
candidate_findings.gap: The algorithm checks every file and directory mtime and deletes old entries. The active-reference check is conditional on feasibility, while pruning may run in the background without a specified lock or revalidation against concurrent writers.
